verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes champagne metal, illumination, and depth as concrete visual-treatment requirements for the wordmark and its signature elements.
The client requires current design artifacts to remain black and white until geometry is resolved and defines the metallic finish as an enhancement rather than the source of the design.
The client explicitly postpones application of the champagne treatment while retaining it as part of the long-term design.
The client assigns confidence to the black silhouette and elevation, light, refinement, and emotional richness to the metallic finish, defining the visual hierarchy between structure and material.
The client specifies a refined champagne-gold finish with warm, restrained, non-flashy visual qualities and limits how the supplied reference may guide the treatment.
The client explicitly resumes material and color exploration after the earlier black-and-white phase.
First target-specific implementation claim after resumption: the freelancer reports rendering four concrete champagne-gold finish variants.
The client narrows the finish candidates and requests concrete selective-distribution and full-gold comparison artifacts.
Distinct target-specific implementation claim: the freelancer reports delivering the newly requested finish-by-distribution comparison grid.
The client identifies Satin Reflection across the three signature elements as the preferred current visual treatment while explicitly leaving finalization pending.
The client ends the project and prohibits further design revisions, removing the still-unfinalized material-treatment obligation.
